notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Yellow front and rear plates are standard; vanity plates are white with blue letters. Only one other southern African country mostly has yellow rear plates.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left, as in much of southern and eastern Africa.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: All coverage uses a white pickup with a short front antenna that always leans slightly left; Oman's similar car leans right.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Most roads have single yellow outer lines and white centre lines, as in neighbouring countries.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Green direction signs with the road number in yellow, again shared with nearby countries.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Road numbers use the letters A, B, C, D, M and sometimes F, while South Africa uses N and R.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: A former central-European colonial power left its mark in place names and in some older buildings.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Small stone bollards stand at intersections and along road sides.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Round metal bins, often painted green and white, sit at many rest stops and intersections; some are blue and white.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: In the north the car is blurred only northwest of Ondangwa; blurred-car coverage correlates with a 2024 copyright.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Tall, lush trees on both sides of the road point north; the more green trees, the further north-northeast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The north around Oshakati has farmland, very light sandy soil and fan palms.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: East of the capital it is flat and dry with slightly reddish soil, short golden grass, shrubs and acacias, like Botswana.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dry mountains and hills dominate the west and south, turning greener with shrubs and trees further northwest.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A pocket south of Tsumeb is the lushest coverage, with fully green grass and mountains.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Sandy coastal landscape with occasional dunes around and north of Swakopmund, and small pockets near Luderitz and Oranjemund.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The southeast has countless small red sandy NW-SE ridges that make roads bumpy like a rollercoaster.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Tall pink sand dunes are found just east of Sossusvlei and can be seen from some roads further away.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: D-road numbers start with 3 digits in the far south and become four-digit numbers starting 1, 2 and then 3 as you move north.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Vineyards are found only around Aussenkehr on the southern border.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Orange thatched fences, walls and huts are everywhere in the desert town of Aussenkehr, built on a hill slope.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Along the C34 coast road, white bollards have two yellow reflectors on the front and a red one on the back.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The B4 east of Luderitz has blindingly bright sandy soil with a railway close on the south side.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The C43 has impressive red tabletop mountains and a wide unpaved road of light gravel.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: The capital has many high-rises downtown, affluent gated houses on hilly streets with simple white street signs, and slums on the northwest hills.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A large desert grid town with red soil, mostly unpaved roads, rare green street signs with silver framing, and blue bins.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The coastal twin towns are flat with sandy streets, palms and Norfolk pines, and square signposts; Swakopmund has yellow lampposts downtown.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A small resort town between the coastal towns has pink brick sidewalks beside nearly every road and always gloomy skies.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A well-off, gridded town with east-west avenues, north-south streets named on small blue markers and many Norfolk pines.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A crown-shaped mountain is faintly visible northwest of Uis, with white open-pit mines to the west.
